title: Specialty Finance Brokerage — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Commercial Deal Underwriting, Retained-Fee Economics, Lender Execution, Licensing Controls, Automation, and Small-Team Launch Readiness

worksheets.title: Opportunity, Deal Underwriting & Counterparty Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Select a commercially viable financing niche before spending money on applications or lender introductions. Document borrower quality, collateral evidence, lender appetite, intermediary authority, and repayment capacity so each proposed placement has a defensible economic purpose and an identifiable execution path.
instructions: Choose one initial commercial financing vertical and define its borrower profile, ticket range, collateral, geography, and repayment source. Separate equipment, receivables, SBA, and bridge opportunities because their documentation, licensing analysis, lender appetite, and closing dependencies differ materially.

Collect borrower documents through a restricted portal, then reconcile identity, ownership, bank activity, liabilities, and requested proceeds. Record the source date and reviewer for every material fact rather than copying unverified statements into a lender submission.

Build the lender matrix from current written criteria and conversations with authorized lender representatives. Include excluded industries, minimum coverage, lien expectations, geographic limits, pricing mechanics, and broker compensation rules before assigning a deal.

Stress the actual repayment source using a documented downside case. For receivables, inspect dilution and customer concentration; for equipment, inspect useful life and liquidation support; for bridge financing, test the exit independently of optimistic appreciation.

Approve a qualified opportunity only after the borrower, proposed lender, and broker relationship pass the documented checks. Assign a named owner to each unresolved condition and prevent automated routing from bypassing missing evidence or geographic restrictions.

fields.name: Initial vertical and commercial use
fields.prompt: Define the first borrower segment, financing product, ticket size, eligible states, and specific use of proceeds. Explain why repeatable documentation and accessible lenders make this segment appropriate for the initial operating team.
fields.example: Start with established packaging manufacturers seeking $300,000 to $900,000 equipment loans in states cleared by the licensing review. Require three operating years, identifiable production equipment, and vendor invoices. Exclude household purchases, speculative inventory, and transactions requiring securities placement.

fields.name: Borrower identity and authority
fields.prompt: List the entity records, ownership information, signing authority, and account ownership evidence required for intake. Identify who verifies discrepancies and distinguish broker verification from the lender's separate customer identification obligations.
fields.example: For Harbor Packaging LLC, obtain formation records, a current registry extract, the operating agreement, and a borrowing resolution naming the authorized signer. Reconcile two owners holding 60% and 40%. Match the disbursement account to the entity and escalate any third-party payment request.

fields.name: Sources, uses, and borrower contribution
fields.prompt: Reconcile the requested loan, borrower cash, vendor invoices, closing costs, and other funding sources. Specify whether fees are financed or separately paid and prevent the same borrower contribution from appearing twice.
fields.example: Equipment costs $600,000, installation costs $25,000, and documented closing charges total $5,000, producing $630,000 of uses. A $500,000 loan plus $130,000 borrower cash balances the schedule. The lender separately pays the broker's $10,000 fee; it is excluded from borrower-funded uses.

fields.name: Repayment capacity and downside case
fields.prompt: Calculate debt service coverage using normalized operating cash flow and all required debt payments. Explain adjustments, exclude unsupported addbacks, and record the downside case that would invalidate the current lender match.
fields.example: Verified annual cash available for debt service is $240,000. Existing payments of $60,000 plus proposed payments of $120,000 produce 1.33 times coverage. A 15% cash-flow reduction leaves $204,000 and 1.13 times coverage, below the selected lender's documented 1.25 minimum.

fields.name: Collateral, liens, and valuation evidence
fields.prompt: Identify collateral ownership, existing liens, valuation source, inspection requirements, and expected lien priority. Explain which lender or closing professional resolves filings and releases before funds move to the seller.
fields.example: The proposed collateral consists of two serial-numbered presses priced at $600,000. An existing blanket lien requires a documented release or subordination acceptable to the new lender. Order the relevant UCC search and obtain written closing instructions; a vendor invoice alone proves neither priority nor value.

fields.name: Receivables eligibility and dilution
fields.prompt: For receivables financing, reconcile aging, disputes, credit memos, related-party balances, and customer concentration. Show the borrowing-base calculation separately from the broker's fee and identify any lender-specific eligibility adjustments.
fields.example: An illustrative ledger has $800,000 in receivables. Remove $100,000 aged beyond the lender limit and $50,000 of disputed invoices, leaving $650,000 eligible. An 80% advance produces $520,000 before other reserves. A 45% customer concentration requires a separate haircut under the selected lender's policy.

fields.name: Lender matrix and documented appetite
fields.prompt: Record each candidate lender's product, state coverage, ticket range, coverage threshold, collateral rules, decision authority, and compensation terms. Date the evidence and define how stale criteria are removed from active matching.
fields.example: Equipment Lender A accepts $250,000 to $1,000,000 requests, requires 1.25 times coverage, and pays a contracted 2% origination fee after funding. Receivables Lender B accepts eligible B2B invoices but excludes construction retainage. Reconfirm both profiles every 30 days and before presenting unusual collateral.

fields.name: Counterparty qualification and concentration
fields.prompt: Verify lender identity, funding authority, references, payment history, and broker-contract terms. Set concentration limits using retained fees and pipeline exposure rather than merely counting lenders with signed introduction agreements.
fields.example: Three verified lenders generated retained fees of $60,000, $40,000, and $20,000 over the trailing year. The first represents 50% of $120,000, exceeding the internal 40% target. Qualify two alternatives, check references, and avoid promising borrower access to uncommitted funding.

fields.name: Product boundary and specialist escalation
fields.prompt: Identify characteristics that move a transaction outside the chosen product lane. Specify escalation for SBA eligibility, consumer-purpose ambiguity, securities features, real-estate licensing questions, and bridge exits dependent on uncommitted refinancing.
fields.example: A borrower requests a $750,000 bridge loan against commercial property with repayment from an unsigned refinance proposal. Require a documented fallback sale analysis and specialist review of state brokerage requirements. Decline to market fractional investor interests through the ordinary commercial-loan workflow.

fields.name: Qualification decision and evidence owner
fields.prompt: State the disposition, supporting evidence, unresolved conditions, responsible reviewer, and next decision date. Distinguish internal qualification from lender credit approval and make borrower communications reflect that distinction accurately.
fields.example: Disposition: qualified for lender discussion, not committed funding. The analyst has verified invoices, ownership, and bank statements. The principal must resolve the blanket lien and downside coverage concern within five business days. No term sheet is represented as a binding credit commitment.

worksheets.completion_gate: Advance only when all ten qualification records identify evidence and an owner, at least two suitable lenders have current criteria, sources equal uses, and unresolved restrictions prevent submission until the responsible reviewer documents resolution.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Defect Reserve & Working-Capital Float
worksheets.purpose: Translate funded placements into retained broker fees, then reconcile those fees to the three canonical operating scenarios. Quantify failed-closing expense, contractual clawbacks, collection delays, and cash runway without treating loan principal, unused credit commitments, or cash reserve transfers as operator earnings.
instructions: Start every calculation with the fee the brokerage is entitled to retain under an executed agreement. Display borrower principal in a separate operational column, and distinguish earned fees, unearned contingent amounts, cash receipts, and potential repayments.

Reproduce Conservative, Base, and Scaled revenue, margin, owner profit, and staffing exactly. Treat the illustrative deal counts and fee rates below as ways to explain those totals, not as additional forecasts supplied by the canonical scorecard.

Separate core monthly overhead from incremental production expense, contractor delivery, partner compensation, and expected loss expense. Explain why total annual expenses can exceed twelve times the stated monthly operating range without changing the canonical profit figures.

Build a cohort reserve from observed defects, failed closings, refund rights, and contractual repayment windows. Distinguish management cash earmarks from accounting expenses so a transfer into a reserve bank account never creates a second deduction.

Stress collection timing, funded volume, and lender concentration before committing additional payroll or marketing. Calculate cash available after restricted amounts and unpaid obligations, then assign a concrete spending response to each downside threshold.

fields.name: Retained fee and principal separation
fields.prompt: Document the contractual fee rate, fee base, responsible payer, earning event, and any external share. Show placement volume only as an operating measure and calculate retained revenue without adding principal.
fields.example: A $1,000,000 funded equipment loan carries a lender-paid 2% broker fee, producing $20,000 retained revenue when the contractual earning conditions are met. The brokerage has no partner split on this deal. The $1,000,000 principal belongs in placement reporting, never in brokerage revenue.

fields.name: Conservative scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile annual revenue, total expense, net margin, owner profit, and team size to the Conservative case. Supply an illustrative funded-deal count and retained fee that multiply exactly to canonical revenue.
fields.example: Twelve funded placements at $10,000 retained fees produce $120,000 revenue. Expenses of $90,000 leave $30,000 annual owner net profit and a 25% net margin. Staffing remains 2 full-time people plus 2 contractors; contractor counts do not imply full-time hours or equal compensation.

fields.name: Base scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile the Base case using exact revenue and profit figures. Separate funded placement volume from retained fees, and explain the average monthly fee production needed without assuming closings arrive evenly.
fields.example: Twenty-eight placements at $20,000 retained fees produce $560,000 annual revenue. Expenses of $364,000 leave $196,000 owner net profit, exactly 35.0%. The team is 2 full-time people plus 2 contractors. Average monthly revenue is $46,666.67, although actual collections follow uneven closing dates.

fields.name: Scaled small-team scenario reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reconcile the Scaled case with the six-person staffing ceiling. Identify the illustrative average retained fee and deal count, and calculate expenses from canonical revenue less canonical owner profit.
fields.example: Forty placements at $25,000 retained fees produce $1,000,000 revenue. Annual expenses of $550,000 leave $450,000 owner net profit and a 45% margin. Staffing is 3 full-time people plus 3 contractors, six people total. Illustrative $1,250,000 loans at 2% explain each fee.

fields.name: Expense bridge and monthly operating range
fields.prompt: Allocate each scenario's expense total among core overhead, incremental delivery costs, and expected loss expense. Keep core monthly overhead within the supplied range and document which costs sit outside that run rate.
fields.example: Conservative expenses are $48,000 core, $30,000 delivery, and $12,000 expected losses. Base expenses are $144,000, $192,000, and $28,000. Scaled expenses are $216,000, $284,000, and $50,000. Core monthly overhead is respectively $4,000, $12,000, and $18,000; these illustrative allocations preserve all canonical totals.

fields.name: Scrub defects and failed-closing cost
fields.prompt: Calculate application preparation cost per funded placement using completed and failed files. Define preventable defects, assign remediation ownership, and place failed-file labor inside the existing expense bridge rather than adding it twice.
fields.example: Forty files enter full packaging, but only 28 fund, a 70% conversion rate. At $600 packaging cost per file, total packaging expense is $24,000, or $857.14 per funded deal. The $7,200 spent on twelve failed files is already included in Base delivery expense.

fields.name: Clawback exposure and reserve mechanics
fields.prompt: Record repayment triggers, exposure windows, probability assumptions, expected loss, and cash earmarks. Explain how the accountant distinguishes contingent fee recognition, refund liabilities, and separate liquidity reserves under the brokerage's accounting policy.
fields.example: A $20,000 collected fee has a contractual 90-day early-default repayment provision. An illustrative 5% full-clawback probability implies $1,000 expected loss. Across 28 comparable placements, $28,000 matches the Base loss assumption. Earmarking $28,000 cash is a liquidity action, not another $28,000 expense.

fields.name: Startup funding and runway
fields.prompt: Allocate startup cash across setup expenses and available working capital. Compare runway with the supplied first-deal timeline, include contractor obligations, and identify the funding gap before accepting a launch budget.
fields.example: A $60,000 launch budget allocates $12,000 to licensing and counsel, $8,000 to systems, $10,000 to insurance and initial acquisition, and $30,000 to working capital. At $12,000 core monthly spend, runway is only 2.5 months before variable costs, shorter than the 3–9 month first-deal range.

fields.name: Collection lag and cash trough
fields.prompt: Model the days between funding, fee entitlement, invoicing, and cleared collection. Calculate the cash trough using actual obligations and exclude pending invoices from spendable cash until payment clears.
fields.example: Starting unrestricted cash is $30,000. Over a 45-day collection delay, core overhead consumes $18,000 and scheduled contractor payments consume $8,000, leaving $4,000. Two earned $20,000 invoices remain receivables until collected; their $40,000 face value cannot finance today's payroll.

fields.name: Break-even, sensitivity, and response
fields.prompt: Calculate contribution per closing, break-even funded volume, and a practical downside response. Reconcile the chosen variable-cost assumption to the Base expense bridge instead of inventing a conflicting margin model.
fields.example: Base variable delivery and expected losses total $220,000, or $7,857.14 per closing. Contribution is $12,142.86 against $144,000 fixed overhead, requiring twelve whole closings to break even. At twenty closings, modeled profit falls to about $98,857; pause new recurring spend if unrestricted cash falls below $24,000.

worksheets.completion_gate: Sign off only when the three cases reconcile to $30,000, $196,000, and $450,000 annual owner net profit, principal is excluded from revenue, cash transfers are not double-counted, and a dated funding plan covers the modeled cash trough.

worksheets.title: Execution, Fee Ledger & Technical QA Pre-Flight
worksheets.purpose: Turn a qualified request into an auditable placement workflow with controlled documents, traceable lender submissions, and reconciled fee records. Establish technical checks that prevent duplicate applications, altered payment instructions, unsupported revenue entries, and silent failures between the CRM, portal, accounting system, and lender communications.
instructions: Assign a permanent deal identifier before requesting sensitive documents. Use that identifier across the CRM, portal, lender submission log, contract folder, and accounting records so reviewers can trace every status change without relying on filenames.

Define entry and exit criteria for each execution stage, including the person responsible for borrower updates. Require evidence of actual lender receipt, decision conditions, and funding confirmation rather than treating an outgoing email as successful execution.

Validate documents for completeness, consistency, date coverage, and authorization before submission. Compare bank activity with reported revenue and debt payments, and escalate discrepancies through a documented process instead of modifying borrower records to improve apparent qualification.

Reconcile the contractual earning event to invoice creation and cash receipt. Keep receivables, contingent compensation, refund exposure, and principal placement statistics distinct so the accounting export cannot inflate retained-fee revenue.

Run duplicate-event, access-control, reconciliation, and recovery tests before enabling production integrations. Record actual test results and unresolved defects, and maintain a manual processing path that preserves the same evidence and authorization requirements.

fields.name: Deal identifier and controlled record
fields.prompt: Specify the unique identifier format, system of record, required fields, and document ownership. Describe how duplicate borrower submissions are detected without merging unrelated facilities or exposing one client's records to another.
fields.example: Create deal identifier SF-2026-0142 in HubSpot and mirror it in the restricted document folder and QuickBooks invoice reference. Match possible duplicates using entity identifier, product, and request date. A second facility receives a new identifier linked to the same verified borrower record.

fields.name: Stage transitions and accountable owners
fields.prompt: Define the ordered execution stages, required evidence, responsible owner, and time target for each transition. Prevent automatic progression when the necessary borrower authorization or lender response is absent.
fields.example: Stages are intake, verified package, lender review, conditional offer, closing preparation, funded, and fee collected. The analyst owns packaging within three business days of complete intake. Only a recorded lender response permits conditional-offer status; only confirmed disbursement permits funded status.

fields.name: Document completeness and discrepancy log
fields.prompt: List required documents by product and define checks for missing periods, inconsistent balances, altered files, and unsigned authorities. Record the discrepancy resolution without overwriting the original borrower submission.
fields.example: The equipment checklist requires three bank statements, two annual tax returns, interim statements, a debt schedule, and vendor invoices. A $22,000 monthly debit missing from the debt schedule triggers clarification. Preserve the original schedule and attach the borrower's corrected version with reviewer and receipt dates.

fields.name: Submission authority and recipient controls
fields.prompt: Record borrower authorization, approved recipients, submission scope, secure delivery method, and confirmation of receipt. Limit document sharing to the particular placement purpose and remove recipients when the lender relationship ends.
fields.example: The borrower authorizes submission to Equipment Lenders A and C for the specified $500,000 request. Send time-limited portal invitations to verified business addresses, not public links. Log lender receipt and disable access after withdrawal under the retention schedule, preserving the submission audit record.

fields.name: Term sheet and closing condition comparison
fields.prompt: Compare proposed terms with approved borrower instructions and the lender's closing checklist. Identify changes in proceeds, payment structure, guarantees, collateral, fees, and conditions that require renewed borrower acknowledgment.
fields.example: The initial proposal offered $500,000 over sixty months; final documents offer $475,000 and require an additional guarantor. The broker highlights the $25,000 proceeds reduction and revised obligations before signing. The borrower must update the sources and uses schedule rather than assume the original terms survived.

fields.name: Funding confirmation and payment verification
fields.prompt: Define acceptable proof of funding and the independent verification process for payment instructions. State who may approve changes and keep borrower principal outside brokerage-controlled accounts unless a separately reviewed arrangement permits custody.
fields.example: Obtain lender confirmation that $500,000 was disbursed to the verified equipment vendor. Confirm any changed bank details through a callback to an independently stored number and require a second reviewer. The broker receives only its contracted $10,000 fee, not the borrower's financing proceeds.

fields.name: Fee ledger and accounting treatment
fields.prompt: Design ledger fields for earning date, payer, retained amount, invoice, collection, repayment exposure, and accounting reference. Explain how bookkeeping follows the adopted revenue policy rather than a CRM status label.
fields.example: For an earned $20,000 fee, record the contract reference, funding evidence, invoice INV-0142, and collection due date. Under the approved accrual policy, debit receivables and credit fee revenue when recognition criteria are satisfied. Collection clears receivables; any refund estimate receives separate accountant review.

fields.name: Integration idempotency and validation
fields.prompt: Specify event identifiers, required payload fields, validation rules, retry handling, and duplicate protection. Define how failed events become visible to an operator before an invoice or borrower notification is repeated.
fields.example: Use the pair SF-2026-0142 and fee-earned-v1 as the invoice idempotency key. Reject events lacking contract reference, currency, or earning evidence. Replay the same event three times in testing and require one invoice. Route failed attempts to a monitored exception queue with an assigned reviewer.

fields.name: Access, retention, and recovery test
fields.prompt: Define role-based access, multifactor authentication, retention ownership, backup protection, and restoration testing. Describe how contractors lose access promptly and how restored records preserve the original audit trail.
fields.example: The analyst accesses assigned files; the bookkeeper accesses fee evidence rather than full borrower tax records. Require multifactor authentication and disable departing contractor accounts the same day. Restore a sample deal into an isolated workspace quarterly and verify document hashes, permissions, and ledger links.

fields.name: Pre-flight acceptance and exception resolution
fields.prompt: Record concrete test cases, expected results, actual outcomes, and accountable defect owners. Define which failures stop automated processing and which permit documented manual handling without weakening evidence requirements.
fields.example: Before activation, test a duplicate invoice event, expired portal link, unauthorized export, missing funding confirmation, and failed accounting connection. Expected results are no duplicate billing, denied access, and visible exceptions. If the accounting test fails, keep invoicing manual until reconciliation passes.

worksheets.completion_gate: Release the workflow only after five documented pre-flight tests pass, a sample deal reconciles from contract through collection, principal never enters fee revenue, and a second reviewer confirms payment-change controls and restricted document access.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract & Outreach Audit
worksheets.purpose: Map the brokerage's actual activities to jurisdiction-specific licensing, disclosure, fair-lending, privacy, outreach, and contract requirements. Convert that analysis into evidence-backed operating restrictions, with separate review for SBA compensation, consumer-report access, mortgage-related activity, and transactions that could involve securities rather than ordinary commercial debt.
instructions: Inventory where the brokerage, borrower, collateral, lender, and outreach recipients are located. Analyze the activities actually performed in each jurisdiction rather than assuming a commercial-purpose label or the lender's license automatically covers the intermediary.

Maintain a dated requirements register with statutory citations, applicability reasoning, evidence, and renewal owners. Check exemptions against their specific conditions, and restrict activity when a required license, filing, disclosure, or contractual permission has not been established.

Review borrower and lender contracts together so compensation, refund rights, exclusivity, representations, data sharing, and dispute provisions remain consistent. Explain all material fee arrangements before the borrower incurs the obligation or accepts the covered offer.

Translate fair-lending and security duties into operational controls covering intake, matching, communications, access, and records. Assign responsibility for notices and retention based on the parties' actual roles rather than copying a lender's policy without examining applicability.

Test outreach and product boundaries before starting campaigns or accepting referrals. Verify suppression handling, contact channels, securities indicators, and SBA-specific documentation, then retain evidence showing why each selected process is permitted for the proposed activity.

fields.name: Jurisdiction and licensing applicability map
fields.prompt: Identify relevant jurisdictions, activity descriptions, license categories, exemption conditions, and evidence owners. Include a concrete statutory reference and explain why lender authorization alone does not resolve the brokerage's obligations.
fields.example: For California activity, analyze the California Financing Law, including Financial Code sections 22004 and 22100, and document whether the proposed brokerage activity requires licensing or satisfies an exemption. Verify lender status separately. Restrict California submissions until the written applicability analysis and required authorization are complete.

fields.name: Commercial financing disclosures
fields.prompt: Identify covered commercial financing offers, transaction thresholds, responsible providers, broker delivery duties, and required timing. Record the applicable state rules rather than assuming one national disclosure template covers every product.
fields.example: Review California Financial Code sections 22800–22805 and New York Financial Services Law sections 801–811 with 23 NYCRR Part 600. For each covered offer, identify the responsible provider and any broker delivery obligations. Preserve the actual disclosure version and evidence of delivery before required acceptance.

fields.name: ECOA, matching rules, and notices
fields.prompt: Map the brokerage's role under ECOA and Regulation B, including nondiscrimination, discouragement, decision participation, notices, and recordkeeping. Specify who owns each applicable duty and test lender matching for prohibited criteria.
fields.example: Review 15 U.S.C. 1691 and 12 CFR Part 1002, including sections 1002.2(l), 1002.4, 1002.9, and 1002.12. A referral-only role differs from credit-decision participation. Exclude protected characteristics from matching, identify the party responsible for applicable notices, and document the business-credit retention rule.

fields.name: Consumer reports and guarantor permissions
fields.prompt: Identify whether any owner or guarantor consumer report is accessed, the permissible purpose, authorization evidence, access restrictions, and notice responsibilities. Distinguish business entity credit information from individual consumer-report data.
fields.example: Before requesting an owner's consumer report, document a permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. 1681b and the provider's required authorization process. Limit access to the assigned reviewer. If report information contributes to an adverse decision, determine applicable duties under 15 U.S.C. 1681m and allocate responsibility explicitly.

fields.name: Information security and incident duties
fields.prompt: Determine applicable financial-information safeguards, privacy obligations, service-provider controls, and incident notifications. Record coverage analysis and implement concrete security measures rather than treating a portal vendor's marketing claims as proof of compliance.
fields.example: Assess coverage under 15 U.S.C. 6801–6809 and 16 CFR Part 314, including any limited exceptions and applicable FTC notification duties. Maintain a written security program, multifactor authentication, encryption, vendor oversight, and incident procedures. Separately evaluate affected residents' state breach-notification requirements using actual incident facts.

fields.name: Broker compensation and contract alignment
fields.prompt: Record payer identity, retained compensation, earning conditions, cancellation treatment, clawback triggers, and fee disclosure timing. Compare borrower and lender agreements for inconsistent statements about independence, exclusivity, and compensation.
fields.example: The lender agreement pays 2% of funded principal within fifteen business days after the earning conditions are satisfied. The borrower engagement discloses lender-paid compensation and no borrower success fee. A ninety-day repayment provision identifies covered events, calculation method, notice procedure, and dispute rights.

fields.name: SBA agent compensation and eligibility
fields.prompt: For SBA placements, identify agent services, compensation source, required disclosures, eligibility review, and lender responsibilities. Use current program instructions and avoid representing ordinary lender interest as SBA authorization.
fields.example: For a proposed $750,000 SBA 7(a) placement, review 13 CFR Part 103, 13 CFR 120.221, current SBA Form 159 instructions, and the applicable SBA operating procedures. Describe each compensated service and payer, check current fee restrictions, and have the lender confirm required agent documentation before closing.

fields.name: Email, telephone, and text outreach
fields.prompt: Document outreach channels, audience sourcing, message claims, suppression controls, and applicable federal and state restrictions. Do not treat a business contact label as universal permission for automated calls or marketing texts.
fields.example: Commercial email follows 15 U.S.C. 7704: accurate headers, appropriate identification, a valid postal address, and functioning opt-out processing within ten business days. Review 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200 before calls or texts, including technology, number type, permission requirements, and state restrictions.

fields.name: Securities and mortgage activity boundary
fields.prompt: Identify proposed activities that require separate securities or mortgage analysis. Record transaction structure, compensation basis, collateral, borrower purpose, and the restriction imposed while a qualified reviewer determines the applicable registration requirements.
fields.example: A sponsor asks the broker to sell fractional interests in a debt pool for transaction-based compensation. Suspend that activity and review 15 U.S.C. 78o(a) and the instrument's securities status. Separately assess mortgage requirements for real-estate-secured placements; commercial purpose does not eliminate every state licensing obligation.

fields.name: Requirements evidence and renewal calendar
fields.prompt: Create an auditable register linking each applicable requirement to evidence, operating restriction, reviewer, renewal date, and affected workflow. Define how legal changes and expired authorizations reach the people responsible for submissions and outreach.
fields.example: The register links each approved state to its analysis, license evidence where required, contract version, and disclosure procedure. Assign a principal and outside counsel reviewer. Set reminders sixty and thirty days before renewal, and disable new affected-state submissions if required authority expires.

worksheets.completion_gate: Proceed only when each active jurisdiction and product has a documented applicability decision, required authorizations are current, fee and outreach documents are approved for their actual use, and securities or mortgage exceptions have an assigned specialist and an enforced activity restriction.

worksheets.title: Automation, Growth Flywheel & Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Build a repeatable acquisition and servicing system around application checklists, evidence-based lender matching, and renewal tracking. Measure funded economics rather than message volume, while preserving borrower choice, controlling lender concentration, and providing manual alternatives when data, integrations, counterparties, or automated recommendations fail.
instructions: Select automation only after documenting the manual decision and evidence requirements. Prioritize checklist completion, lender eligibility filtering, and renewal reminders because these reduce repetitive work without delegating credit approval or legal interpretation to an unreviewed software rule.

Build a referral and outbound funnel with explicit stage definitions and denominators. Measure qualified applications, complete packages, funded placements, retained fees, and acquisition cost so booked meetings cannot conceal poor borrower fit or persistent closing failures.

Use named system owners and versioned matching criteria. Capture why lenders were included or excluded, review stale profiles, and require human review for borderline cases rather than allowing automation to fabricate missing financial information or imply guaranteed approval.

Track concentration using both realized retained fees and upcoming closing exposure. Maintain qualified alternatives for important products, and define the borrower communication, rerouting authorization, and cash response triggered by a lender pause or commission dispute.

Review growth experiments and automation exceptions weekly using an evidence log. Expand only when marginal acquisition economics, document quality, staff capacity, and cash collection remain acceptable; stop channels that create complaints, unsuitable applications, or unmanageable sensitive-data exposure.

fields.name: Ideal customer and acquisition proposition
fields.prompt: Define the borrower profile, observable trigger event, financing need, acquisition channel, and evidence-backed service promise. Exclude claims of certain approval, universal lender coverage, or pricing that cannot be supported for the target segment.
fields.example: Target packaging manufacturers adding a production line within six months and seeking $300,000 to $900,000 equipment financing. Lead with organized documentation and comparison of suitable lender structures. Promise a completeness review within two business days, not a funding decision or a fixed interest rate.

fields.name: Referral partner qualification and economics
fields.prompt: Identify referral sources, permitted activities, compensation conditions, borrower disclosures, and lead-quality standards. Confirm whether partner conduct creates licensing or agent issues before exchanging applications or paying transaction-linked compensation.
fields.example: Recruit three equipment dealers and two accountants for introductions. Initially use uncompensated referrals with borrower-authorized contact sharing. If a compensated arrangement is proposed, review applicable licensing and disclosure rules first, then document the fee and include it in delivery expense rather than hiding it inside principal.

fields.name: Funnel mathematics and stage definitions
fields.prompt: Calculate a complete funnel using one consistent cohort and time window. Define each stage, show conversion rates, and reconcile funded deal counts to the illustrative Base retained-fee model.
fields.example: An annual planning cohort contains 400 eligible contacts, 100 substantive conversations, 60 applications, 40 complete packages, and 28 funded deals. Stage conversions are 25%, 60%, 66.67%, and 70%. At $20,000 retained per funding, the final stage produces the canonical $560,000 Base revenue.

fields.name: Application checklist automation
fields.prompt: Specify checklist triggers, product-specific requirements, reminder cadence, exception handling, and human review. Explain how the automation detects missing evidence without inventing document contents or repeatedly requesting already accepted files.
fields.example: A HubSpot stage change creates the equipment checklist in the secure portal. Reminder tasks run after three and seven business days for missing items only. The analyst reviews mismatched statement periods. Once a file is accepted, its status suppresses further reminders unless a documented refresh requirement applies.

fields.name: Lender matching rules and explainability
fields.prompt: Define hard eligibility filters, ranking factors, evidence freshness, and reviewer overrides. Keep compensation separate from suitability and record the reason for each recommendation so borrower interests are visible in the process.
fields.example: Filter first by authorized geography, product, $500,000 ticket size, industry, collateral, and required coverage. Rank surviving lenders by structure fit and documented execution performance. Do not rank solely by broker fee. An override requires the principal's written reason and a current lender confirmation of the exception.

fields.name: Renewal tracking and borrower service
fields.prompt: Define renewal, maturity, covenant, and document-refresh dates with accountable owners. Explain how reminders improve borrower service without treating uncommitted refinancing or future fees as recognized revenue.
fields.example: For a receivables facility renewing on September 30, schedule borrower contact 120 days earlier and updated aging collection 90 days earlier. Review concentration and renewal terms sixty days before maturity. Any potential renewal fee stays in forecast reporting until the contractual earning conditions are satisfied.

fields.name: Acquisition cost and experiment budget
fields.prompt: Calculate acquisition cost using attributable spending and funded cohort results. Distinguish early leading indicators from mature economics and set a spending threshold consistent with the existing expense model.
fields.example: A mature campaign costs $18,000 and produces six funded placements, yielding $3,000 acquisition cost per funding. At $20,000 retained fees, gross retained fees before other costs are $120,000. Include campaign spending within Base delivery expense; cap the next unproven test at $2,000.

fields.name: Lender concentration and interruption fallback
fields.prompt: Measure concentration by trailing retained revenue and expected pipeline fees. Define an interruption trigger, alternative lenders, borrower permissions, and the cash-management response if the largest counterparty stops funding.
fields.example: Lender A represents $224,000 of $560,000 Base revenue, or 40%, and six pending files carrying $120,000 potential fees. A funding pause triggers alternative-lender review within two business days, renewed borrower authorization before redistribution, and suspension of discretionary acquisition spend until collection exposure is reassessed.

fields.name: Integration failure and manual fallback
fields.prompt: List critical integration dependencies, failure signals, response owners, manual procedures, and reconciliation requirements. Ensure fallback handling preserves recipient restrictions and avoids duplicate lender submissions or invoices.
fields.example: If the CRM-to-portal connection fails for thirty minutes, the operations owner opens a controlled exception register. Staff create portal tasks manually using existing deal identifiers. On restoration, compare event identifiers and task records before replaying messages; never resend sensitive attachments through ordinary email to bypass the outage.

fields.name: Weekly learning loop and stop criteria
fields.prompt: Define the weekly review agenda, experiment evidence, complaint tracking, defect thresholds, and improvement ownership. Specify which findings stop an acquisition channel or require changes before additional spend.
fields.example: Every Friday, review contact quality, application completion, funding conversion, collection lag, complaints, and exceptions. Pause a channel if more than 20% of its last twenty applications misstate the permitted use of funds. Assign one corrective experiment and review the next twenty applications before restoring the previous budget.

worksheets.completion_gate: Activate growth automation only after the funnel reconciles, matching explanations are recorded, suppression and duplicate controls pass testing, renewal forecasts remain outside earned revenue, and a named owner has rehearsed the largest-lender and integration-outage fallback procedures.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch, Pod KPI Scorecard & Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Translate the operating design into a thirty-day launch sequence with accountable owners, measured capacity, and cash-aware milestones. Preserve clean contracts, financial records, and counterparty evidence from the start so the brokerage can support disciplined growth, continuity planning, and a later diligence process.
instructions: Treat the first thirty days as a readiness and pipeline-building sprint, not a promise of funded revenue. The supplied first-deal range is three to nine months, so sequence spending against available capital and verified execution progress.

Assign each launch deliverable to one accountable person and identify any specialist dependency. Preserve the Base team design of two full-time people and two contractors, while checking actual workload and employment classification rather than assuming headcount alone proves capacity.

Review a compact weekly scorecard covering qualified demand, complete packages, funding conversion, retained fees, collection lag, defects, concentration, and cash. Define each denominator and owner so metric changes represent operating facts rather than shifting definitions.

Build the diligence ledger alongside ordinary operations. Preserve executed contracts, license evidence, fee reconciliations, clawback cohorts, security records, and assignment restrictions without exposing borrower records to prospective counterparties before appropriate authorization and controlled access.

At the end of the sprint, compare completed evidence with the plan and make a documented proceed, remediate, or pause decision. List unfinished work explicitly, maintain cash discipline, and separate readiness accomplishments from transactions that have actually funded.

fields.name: Launch charter and canonical positioning
fields.prompt: State the candidate, pipeline rank, leverage score, capital range, operating range, and first-deal timeline. Explain how these inputs shape the launch rather than treating the score as earned performance.
fields.example: Volume 014 covers Candidate #20, Specialty Finance Brokerage, ranked #06 of 29 with a 89/100 Money-to-Manpower Score: 23 revenue, 21 margin, 17 team efficiency, 8 accessibility, and 10 automation. Plan around $20,000–$100,000 startup capital, $4,000–$18,000 monthly core operations, and three to nine months to the first deal.

fields.name: Days 1–7: scope, authority, and evidence
fields.prompt: Define the first week's deliverables, accountable owners, budget limits, and dependencies. Prioritize product scope, jurisdiction analysis, contract review, and secure intake before purchasing broad acquisition capacity.
fields.example: The principal selects equipment finance for established packaging manufacturers, commissions the initial jurisdiction review, and approves draft engagements. The analyst configures restricted intake and the lender matrix. Cap first-week committed setup spending at $6,000 within the broader $60,000 launch allocation and record each signed obligation.

fields.name: Days 8–14: counterparties and dry runs
fields.prompt: Specify lender qualification, workflow tests, sample documentation, and training deliverables for the second week. Use synthetic test files rather than distributing real borrower information without authorization.
fields.example: Qualify three equipment lenders using verified contacts, written appetite, and broker agreements. Run two clearly labeled synthetic applications through checklist and matching tests without submitting them as real credit requests. Complete duplicate-invoice, access-denial, and backup-restoration tests before enabling live borrower intake.

fields.name: Days 15–21: controlled acquisition pilot
fields.prompt: Define the pilot audience, channel, contact limits, spending cap, success criteria, and stop conditions. Measure early pipeline quality without claiming that conversations or applications already represent funded revenue.
fields.example: Contact forty verified business prospects and hold five referral-partner conversations through reviewed channels. Cap pilot spending at $2,000 within the initial acquisition allocation. Target ten substantive borrower conversations and four eligible applications; record zero earned fees until actual contractual earning conditions have been satisfied.

fields.name: Days 22–30: execution rehearsal and review
fields.prompt: List final sprint deliverables, evidence owners, cash review, and unresolved work. Distinguish completed readiness tests from live underwriting outcomes and define the next operating period's spending permission.
fields.example: Complete two authorized lender submissions if borrower files qualify, reconcile the cash ledger, and rehearse the largest-lender interruption scenario. If licensing work remains open, continue internal preparation but restrict affected submissions. Approve the next month's spending only after reviewing remaining runway and documented obligations.

fields.name: Pod responsibilities and capacity calculation
fields.prompt: Allocate responsibilities across full-time and contractor roles, estimate hours per file, and identify bottlenecks. Compare capacity with the Base funnel while preserving separation of duties for sensitive changes.
fields.example: The principal owns lender relationships and exceptions; the analyst owns packaging and borrower updates. Two contractors cover bookkeeping and specialist file support. Forty annual packages at eighteen analyst hours require 720 hours, before follow-up and renewals. Payment-detail changes still require two independent reviewers.

fields.name: Weekly KPI scorecard and escalation
fields.prompt: Define target metrics, formulas, data sources, owners, and escalation thresholds. Separate mature annual planning assumptions from early sprint observations so small samples do not create false operating certainty.
fields.example: Track complete packages divided by applications, funded deals divided by mature completed packages, retained fees, median collection days, defect rate, and unrestricted cash. Base planning uses 28 fundings from forty packages. Escalate collection delays beyond thirty days past contractual due dates and any unresolved identity discrepancy.

fields.name: Owner-profit bridge and distribution discipline
fields.prompt: Connect the canonical profit cases to the management ledger and cash distribution policy. Separate accounting profit from collectible cash and retain funding for obligations, loss exposure, and continued operations.
fields.example: The annual reference cases remain $120,000 revenue and $30,000 profit; $560,000 and $196,000; and $1,000,000 and $450,000. These are not monthly draw budgets. If Base profit accrues while $40,000 remains uncollected, review receivables, unpaid expenses, repayment exposure, and required working capital before authorizing an owner distribution.

fields.name: Exit-readiness and transferable evidence
fields.prompt: List diligence records that demonstrate earnings quality, counterparty durability, operating independence, and transfer restrictions. Explain how a prospective buyer receives staged access without unnecessary disclosure of borrower documents.
fields.example: Maintain monthly fee reconciliations, funding cohorts, clawback history, lender concentration, executed contracts, license records, and procedure versions. Index assignment and change-of-control clauses because lender agreements and licenses may require separate action. Begin diligence with aggregated metrics and redacted samples in a restricted data room.

fields.name: Day-30 decision and next-period commitments
fields.prompt: Record the proceed, remediate, or pause decision with evidence, cash available, unresolved risks, accountable owners, and dated next actions. Avoid declaring completion for work that remains untested or dependent on another party.
fields.example: Decision: remediate before expanding. Three lender profiles are verified and two workflow rehearsals passed, but one state review remains open. Unrestricted cash is $26,000 against $12,000 monthly core spend. The principal resolves the state question within ten business days; acquisition stays capped and no funded revenue is reported.

worksheets.completion_gate: Close the sprint only after every milestone has an evidenced status, the pod accepts its responsibilities, the scorecard uses stable definitions, cash reconciles to the ledger, and the day-30 decision explicitly identifies unfinished work, funding needs, and restrictions on further activity.
